title: Explicit private-contact submission identity derivation boundary
purpose: Derive explicit canonical contact identities deterministically from an independently supplied opaque submission token without issuing tokens or authorizing execution.
phase: Specification only; implementation and test changes require a later explicit instruction.
inputs: An independently supplied opaque submissionToken value, accepted as unknown and validated as canonical nonempty string evidence
output: An object containing attemptId: InsuranceContactAttemptId and idempotencyKey: InsuranceContactIdempotencyKey; invalid token evidence throws without side effects.
requirements: Implement a synchronous pure helper accepting only the independently supplied submission token.

Require typeof submissionToken to be string, require nonzero length, and require submissionToken.trim() === submissionToken. Reject missing, null, non-string, empty, blank, or normalization-changing evidence rather than repairing it.

Canonical token text in this slice means nonempty text with no leading or trailing whitespace. Treat its remaining content as opaque; introduce no UUID, character-set, case-folding, Unicode-normalization, or maximum-length rule in this slice.
Construct attemptId exactly as contact-attempt:<token> and validate it through createInsuranceContactAttemptId.
Construct idempotencyKey exactly as private-contact:<token> and validate it through createInsuranceContactIdempotencyKey.
Reuse existing InsuranceContactAttemptId and InsuranceContactIdempotencyKey types through type-only imports; do not duplicate identity grammars or substitute quote-request identity validation rules.
The same accepted token must deterministically produce the same identity pair, and distinct accepted tokens must produce distinct pairs. Preserve token content exactly in both identities.

Never generate a token, random value, timestamp, retry key, or fallback identity internally. Do not derive identity solely from relationship, channel, or intent, and do not accept those fields as inputs.
Do not mutate inputs, normalize accepted token content, or maintain process-local identity state.

This slice does not establish token provenance, browser/session retention, persistence, exactly-once delivery, or execution authorization. It does not guarantee that an external issuer supplies unique tokens or retains them across retries.

Accept no provider, database, transport, route runtime, persistence factory, or orchestration service. Do not call requestContact, read or write persistence, or perform network or filesystem operations.
Leave the private route, both existing provider-not-configured no-store 503 responses, INS-007Y/Z, contact orchestration, and existing identity validators unchanged.
tests: A valid opaque token produces exactly contact-attempt:<token> and private-contact:<token> through the existing validators.
Repeated calls with the same token return equivalent pairs; distinct tokens, including case-distinct tokens, return distinct pairs.
Missing, undefined, null, non-string, empty, and whitespace-only token evidence rejects without generating fallback identities.
Leading/trailing whitespace token evidence rejects rather than being trimmed; accepted opaque content is preserved exactly.
Returned identities are compatible with createInsuranceContactAttemptId and createInsuranceContactIdempotencyKey and their existing branded types.

Frozen holder input containing a primitive token remains unchanged when its token is supplied; repeated calls remain deterministic without mutable state. Frozen object tokens themselves reject as non-string evidence.

Source isolation permits only local token validation, deterministic prefix construction, and existing identity validators; no runtime/provider dependency, contact execution, persistence, transport, random generation, timestamp generation, or relationship/channel/intent derivation.
boundaries: This phase creates this specification only; no implementation or test mutation.
No route changes or replacement of either existing 503 response.
No persistence writes, token issuance, browser/session retention mechanism, or provider/runtime access.
No requestContact execution, live call, SMS, email, or provider activation.
No migrations, deployment, billing, routing, scoring, producer assignment, second CRM, Sesh, or unrelated changes.
nextBoundary: Token provenance and issuance, retry retention and lifecycle, request binding, concurrency/recovery guarantees, route integration, and contact execution authorization remain separately defined and explicitly authorized work. Derived identities alone never enable live contact.
